evidence.notes: R-related to EI-10717 (see its note) — the ATTRIBUTION half: apps/operator-vite owns a typecheck ratchet that counts FOREIGN errors from packages it imports but does not own, so an error introduced in operator-core reds a stranger's gate and lands on whoever next touches operator-vite. PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED, deliberately NOT discarded: the specific mechanism this item asked for — operator-core having a typecheck of its own — now EXISTS as `npm run lint:tsc` (scripts/lint-tsc.mjs:167, `tsc -p packages/operator-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so operator-core errors are catchable at their own boundary. What I did NOT verify is whether lint:tsc is ENFORCED anywhere automatic (a green-checkpoint gate step, a CI job) as opposed to being a lever agents are told to run by hand. That distinction decides the whole item: an unenforced typecheck does not stop a foreign error from reaching operator-vite's ratchet, so the attribution defect would survive its own fix. Merit left UNTRIAGED for exactly that reason rather than guessed in either direction.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## The symptom
The rig (Lm1ABoMR), running a bundle that CONTAINS fix C (composedAt 2026-07-27T11:44:22Z), receives the canonical key in a refusal every single tick and never adopts it:

```
[2026-07-27T11:51:22.768Z] [git-sync] papercusp: ref-announce receive fetch FAILED for
IXfGu216EI/z (event 441080); holding cursor at 440845 to re-dial next tick:
no git process ran: duplex error: pot-git serve refused: superseded-repo-key:gh-1223568103
```

Five of these in a single tick. The correct canonical key `gh-1223568103` is sitting in the error text. Nothing adopts it. The rig's `papercusp.git` still holds ZERO namespaces.

## The root cause — reachability, not logic
`adoptRefusedRepoKey` is correct and well-guarded. It has exactly ONE production call site:

- `git-sync-action.ts:2034` — inside the BOOTSTRAP leg's dial path.

But the refusal that carries the repair arrives on a DIFFERENT leg: the ref-announce RECEIVE leg (`git-sync-action.ts:~2345`, the `cursorDecision.fetchFailed` loop). That loop has `f.stderr` containing the verbatim refusal text — and does nothing with it but `console.warn`.

So the one channel on which the repair reliably and repeatedly arrives is the one channel that cannot act on it.

## Why this is the mirror image of fix D
Fix D's own comment (git-sync-action.ts:1839) says the probe must sit ABOVE the warm gate because "a probe placed after the gate would never fire on precisely the machine that needs it: the stuck one." Fix C has the same defect in a different dimension: its receiver is on the cold-join path, so it never runs on the machine whose ref-announce leg is the thing actually dialing.

## The fix
Call `adoptRefusedRepoKey` from the ref-announce receive leg's fetchFailed handler, using `f.stderr` — the same fail-soft, next-tick-effective contract the bootstrap call site already uses. Adoption is idempotent (`already-canonical` is a clean no-op on every later refused dial), so calling it from both legs is safe by construction.

## Broader lesson (worth keeping)
A REFUSAL THAT CARRIES ITS OWN REPAIR ONLY HEALS IF EVERY LEG THAT CAN RECEIVE IT KNOWS HOW TO READ IT. Wiring the receiver into one leg makes the feature look done and tested while leaving it inert on the live path.
_claimSubjectBaseline.title: RELEASE BLOCKER (fix C reachability): adoptRefusedRepoKey has ONE call site, on the bootstrap DIAL path — but the superseded-repo-key refusal actually arrives every tick on the REF-ANNOUNCE receive leg, which only logs it. The self-heal rides in on a channel with no receiver, so the tower<->rig pair cannot heal.

evidence.notes: ELECTED SURVIVOR of the pair. FINDING: on the Mac rig (hello-world-3-pot) the outbox re-wire path spins without any backoff and wedges the pot — measured 2026-08-09 at ~32 Hz with a 68,003,634-byte log growing 1,295 lines/10s, the last 4,000 lines a single 4-line cycle repeated 988 times, pot permanently unreachable. R-remedy rather than R-finding: its sibling EI-21157761175098740 reports the same unbacked-off re-wire spin (~2,850/min) on the same rig but attributes it to a DIFFERENT trigger — a hypercore own-log FORK (own_log_forked, conflict detected in own log) rather than this item's SESSION_CLOSED outbox path — so the remedies diverge at the trigger even though the pathology is identical. THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ABOUT THIS PAIR IS THE 13-DAY GAP: two independent sightings on the same rig, 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-22, prove the defect was never fixed between them, and the fact that two DIFFERENT triggers produce the same runaway says the durable defect is the MISSING BACKOFF, not either trigger. Fixing whichever trigger is diagnosed first will leave the class armed for the next one — the repo's own rule that a mitigation is not a fix applies exactly here. Provenance=argued: this is a remote rig I cannot query from this harness, so both reports rest on their authors' measurements; the corroboration between them is strong but is not my own verification.

evidence.notes: PREMISE VERIFIED AND THE DEFECT IS LARGER THAN FILED. The item reports that sibling work-items can share one payload.plan_item stamp, so completing a SUB-LANE child flips its PARENT's plan item to done via finishPlanStamp(), and states 126 plan items affected with 51 still live. Measured 2026-08-22 over harness_shared.work_items in papercusp-workspace: 4,602 stamped rows across 4,337 distinct (plan_slug,item_id) stamps, of which 200 stamps are SHARED by more than one row, spanning 465 rows, and 83 of those shared stamps still have at least one live (non-done/dropped/deprecated) sibling. So the true figures are 200 affected stamps (filed: 126) and 83 with a live sibling (filed: 51) — the filer UNDER-CLAIMED by ~1.6x on both. That is the THIRD independent confirmation of D-026 s4's direction-of-error rule, on a third unrelated finding, and it is now safe to treat "a filed number is a floor to re-measure" as established rather than suggestive. R-related to EI-20577421906951067, not a duplicate: this one is the OVER-FIRE (things get closed that should not be), that one is the IRREVERSIBILITY (a wrong closure cannot be undone). They are two halves of one trap and neither is safe to fix alone — fixing only the over-fire leaves existing bad closures stuck; fixing only the reopen path leaves the source of them running. Both are complaints against the very reconciler whose existence supersedes EI-2443/EI-2725 in this same batch.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
DIRECT FOLLOW-UP to EI-23345472964244980 (closed 2026-09-16), which built the per-tool argSchema byte budget + the two seed wire guards and established the headline: the core MCP spine is 353,380 B in-repo against D-001's 262,144 B ceiling (34.8% over), with 8 of 48 names = 55% of it. That item MEASURED and GUARDED the breach. This one is about CUTTING it, and it starts by killing the obvious wrong answer.

=== NEGATIVE RESULT FIRST — DO NOT SPEND A SESSION ON THIS ===
The natural fix is 'the whales inline the same nested payload twice, so switch the converter to emit $defs/$ref'. Concretely: libs/generic/tooldef/src/schema-adapter.ts calls z.toJSONSchema(schema) with NO options, and Zod 4 defaults `reused` to 'inline'. Flipping it to 'ref' looks like a one-line catalog-wide win.

IT IS REFUTED, on two independent grounds, both measured 2026-09-16:

1. MEASURED WORSE on the population that could be re-converted. Over the 67 tools still carrying their zod `args`, reused:'ref' produced 68,805 B vs 58,201 B inline — 18.2% BIGGER. 48 of 67 grew by exactly +51 B: the $defs wrapper overhead with no actual reuse to amortize. (That sample contains no whale, so it does not by itself settle the whales — ground 2 does.)

2. STRUCTURALLY INCOMPATIBLE WITH THE PROJECTION. libs/generic/tooldef/src/define-tool.ts:1298 `flattenForOpenAi` DELIBERATELY flattens root-level oneOf/anyOf into one merged object, because LLM clients cannot accept a root union in a tool inputSchema. The projection's whole job is to FLATTEN. Emitting $defs/$ref would fight that pass, not cooperate with it. The inlining is intentional, not an oversight.

Also worth knowing for any future probe: the projected registry (listAllProjectedTools(), 889 tools) carries ONLY the already-converted `inputSchema` — zero of the 889 retain the zod `args`, so you cannot re-convert from it. The zod source survives only in the legacy getCatalog() catalog, and importing that from @papercusp/agent-mcp in a scratch probe returned just 67 tools (a different module record — the documented singleton-split trap). Measure composition from `inputSchema`; it needs no zod.

=== WHERE THE BYTES ACTUALLY ARE (in-repo projection, 889 tools) ===
TOTAL 1,216,782 B, of which DESCRIPTION PROSE = 627,429 B = 51.6%.

name                          total    prose  prose%
work_items:complete           43,283   21,714    50%
coord:send                    38,185   29,305    77%
rubrics:propose               36,402   20,074    55%
rubrics:amend                 27,927   14,602    52%
work_items:checkpoint         23,358   16,477    71%
fleet:launch-on-plan          21,940   17,421    79%
loop:checkpoint               20,174   14,008    69%
improvements:capture          19,033   12,175    64%
scorecards:emit               17,743    6,967    39%
facts:assert                  14,452   11,603    80%
capability:launch-agent       11,262    8,100    72%
work_items:create             10,778    6,195    57%

So the dominant lever is PROSE, not structure — and it is ungoverned: the existing tool-weight promptWeight budget measures the tool's own `description` + `guidance` fields, NOT the .describe() strings inside the argSchema. A tool can sit comfortably inside its prompt budget while shipping 29 KB of schema prose on every tools/list (coord:send does exactly that: 1,356 chars of prompt weight, 38,185 B of argSchema).

=== THE MULTIPLIER, which changes the ranking ===
work_items:complete top-level properties: items=21,921 B, completion=17,235 B, specAdequacy=2,945 B, everything else <310 B. `completion` and `items[].completion` are the SAME completionSpec, serialized twice (single-shorthand branch + items[] batch branch, merged by flattenForOpenAi). So every byte of prose inside completionSpec is paid TWICE — a 1-char trim there saves 2 bytes. Any tool offering a single shorthand beside an items[] batch has this doubling; that is the shared shape behind several whales.

=== PROPOSED WORK, cheapest and least-risky first ===
1. TRIM PROSE in the top whales' argSchemas, prioritising the doubled nested specs (completionSpec first — 2x yield per byte). Pure prose editing: reversible, no contract change, no client-compat question, and it is the same discipline the repo already applies to tool description/guidance — prefer a docs pointer over prose-in-place. Rough ceiling if the top 12 alone went from ~65% prose to ~30%: on the order of 60-70 KB in-repo, which reads HIGHER on the wire (in-repo runs ~20-35% below live).
2. EXTEND THE GOVERNANCE so this cannot regrow: the new SCHEMA_BYTE_BUDGET from EI-23345472964244980 caps total argSchema bytes per tool, but nothing caps the PROSE FRACTION. A prose-share signal in `npm run tool-weight` would make the 77%/80% outliers visible at edit time rather than at the gate.
3. ONLY THEN consider de-duplicating the single/batch pairing (e.g. advertising the items[] form alone while the existing z.preprocess hoisting — hoistMisplacedCompletionFields / gatherFlatCompletion — keeps flat single calls working at runtime). This one IS a real contract/discoverability change to the fleet's highest-traffic finish verb, so it wants a plan Decision and peer sign-off, not a unilateral edit. Listed last deliberately.

EVIDENCE: probes .papercusp/scratch/reused-ref-win.mts and .papercusp/scratch/whale-composition.mts (gitignored scratch; both re-runnable with `npx tsx <path>`, they load the agent-tools barrel and process.exit(0) — note the documented 'barrel hangs under bare tsx' is really just the barrel's listeners holding the event loop open, which the explicit exit resolves).

ⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts` (32 newer commits, tip `8624ebc8dc74ea542338bf1f9218922ced88bc3d`), `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/send.ts` (5 newer commits, tip `60fd7a89a65540dcd8da92db661aefd61222ffdf`) have commits newer than the running build (`e66be3c4ff`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.
_claimSubjectBaseline.title: 51.6% of the catalog's 1.22 MB argSchema wire cost is .describe() PROSE (627 KB) — ungoverned; and the $ref fix is refuted, the lever is prose + the single/batch duplication

New targeted papercusp-dev-api.service logs show the sentinel reported STALLED at 02:58:57.896Z after 10,018ms (main thread spinning, state R, 0.99 cores, CPU PSI some60=5.4), then SIGKILLed request-worker PID 2970199 at 02:59:11.910Z after 24,031ms (mode kill, 20,000ms threshold, 0.98 cores, PSI=5.77). At 02:59:22 a PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0 secondary host booted; the live systemd operator unit nRestarts=0 supports worker respawn without a unit restart, so the title remains accurate. Same-window bounded-timeout lines for turn-start executable frontier and agent-obligations show slow work but do not identify a caller; system journal had no OOM/hung-task/lockup matches. This establishes a nearby request-worker CPU-spin class, not exact linkage to the earlier 02:57 sample or the JS frame. The prior carry-note statement that 02:50–03:05Z had zero service-journal entries was wrong. The worker is gone, so its JS stack cannot be recovered. No code change is justified from this trace alone: on the next recurrence, act on the first STALLED line (~10s stale), send SIGUSR1 to the reported Node PID, capture /json/list and a 3–5s V8 sampling profile before the 20s kill threshold, plus per-thread /proc state/wchan/cgroup and unit+system journals. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
EI-24740170321140267 and EI-24741224734319108 document staging-api remaining in systemd start-pre with MainPID=0 and no :3170 listener, including a wait exceeding 30 minutes. EI-24741366548405319 independently reproduces immediate ECONNREFUSED from ptool tools:find at :3170 while the attributed :3271 helper remains reachable. EI-24741649901659036 reports the same endpoint-level condition through a TCP preflight: nothing is listening. The common mechanism is staging-service startup failing to attain availability, so unrelated valid MCP tools fail before their handlers run. Investigate the pre-start lifecycle and verify listener readiness; the precise startup blocker or lock holder is not established.

Shared-root-cause evidence: Startup-state reports, a valid discovery-call reproduction and an independent service-health check converge on the absent staging listener, rather than separate tool-handler defects.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Owner directive #85 from Avi, verbatim: "Can you cut and publish a 0.0.22 release off of the latest green main? These build cuts should always come from the latest green main unless explicitly said otherwise". The second sentence is a STANDING convention, recorded as workspace fact `release-cuts-come-from-latest-green-main` (kind:convention, no expiry) — it outlives this task.

MEASURED SO FAR (su-c03852cb, 2026-09-22T14:53Z):
- GREEN MAIN SHA = be8396c6ddc0f9cc8f81eea784320e0cd24cf8fd. local main == origin/main (verified equal). main is automation-only and only fast-forwards on a green checkpoint, so its tip IS the latest green by construction. Corroboration: the running :3070 operator self-reports build be8396c6dd, i.e. the deployed green matches this sha.
- Current version on disk = 0.0.21, so 0.0.22 is the correct increment.
- Previous cut (0.0.21) COMPLETED: release:cut{op:status} -> state done, exitCode 0, 6 signed artifacts, local tag desktop-v0.0.21-alpha (NOT pushed).
- No peer is doing this. su-77b3a99d recorded the same convention fact 4min before me but is on WI-10002411 (gate red); nobody's declared intent mentions the release.

THE PIPELINE (from release:cut's own output + tool description):
1. release:cut{op:preflight} REFUSED from the canonical tree: `root_not_isolated — default cut root is auto-managed and can move during a build; prepare a dedicated exact-SHA worktree with setup-release-checkout.sh and pass it via root`. So step 1 is standing up that worktree at apps/operator/bin/release/setup-release-checkout.sh, pinned to be8396c6dd.
2. release:cut{op:run, root, version:'0.0.22', channel, sourceSha:be8396c6dd…, ownerName} — sourceSha is REQUIRED and drift refuses before writes. Expect a LONG build (0.0.21 ran 10:06→11:17Z).
3. papercusp-desktop/bin/verify-provenance.sh <leg-out-dir> --health-sha <sha> --require-signed per leg.
4. release:cut{op:handoff, version} to collect artifacts.
5. PUBLISH via papercusp-desktop/bin/upload-release.sh (reads the artifact manifest release:cut writes).

⛔ HARD CONSTRAINT from the tool description: artifacts stay LOCAL and the cut itself must NEVER create a GitHub Release. op:prepare-tag is the separate, explicit remote-ref write. Do not conflate 'publish' with the cut auto-pushing anything — 0.0.21's tag was deliberately local and unpushed.

OPEN QUESTION to resolve before op:run: CHANNEL. 0.0.21 was cut as `alpha` (tag desktop-v0.0.21-alpha), but stable|beta|alpha are all valid and a beta release-history page exists (EI-23963957634267483). Defaulting to `alpha` for continuity with the immediately preceding cut unless evidence says otherwise; disclosing the choice to Avi rather than asking.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## Observed (measured 2026-09-22T19:10Z, su-4efe1c00)
This session's carry-respawn continuation arrived as `<pasted_content id="5f47">\n⟦turn-origin:self-compaction nonce:807623f407ac1ff3⟧ ADDRESSED TO su-4efe1c00… </pasted_content>`. The UserPromptSubmit hook stamped it `⟦turn-provenance⟧ OWNER (interactive) — no origin envelope, no ledger match` and the directive-capture rail recorded it as PENDING owner order #140 (the prior respawn's continuation had likewise become #128). Both were dismissed by me as machine-origin.

## Fleet-wide scale (measured, orders:list open:true at 19:12Z)
16 open orders; the carry excerpts of #127, #128, #130, #132, #134, #135 (self-compaction), #131, #133 (wake-pump) and #136, #137 (fleet-kickoff, recorded by role-* grading auditors) all begin `<pasted_content id=…>\n⟦turn-origin:…⟧` — i.e. machine-injected turns captured as owner directives, ~10 in ~20 minutes across ~9 sessions.

## Cause (measured in code)
`packages/operator-core/lib/turn-provenance/envelope-grammar.ts:67` — `ENVELOPE_PATTERN_SOURCE = ^\s*⟦turn-origin:(…) nonce:(…)⟧` is START-anchored; `parseEnvelope` (turn-provenance.ts:149) uses it, so a `<pasted_content …>` prefix defeats the match. `grep -rl pasted_content` over scripts/, packages/operator-core/lib, apps/operator/lib → 0 files: no code unwraps the wrapper. The ledger-hash fallback also misses (wrapped text ≠ injected payload), so classify() falls through to the final OWNER branch (turn-provenance.ts:671).
[inferred, not probed] The `<pasted_content>` wrapper is added by the Claude Code client when a long prompt is delivered as input; the injectors send a correctly-enveloped payload.

## Why major
1. Manufactures owner directives out of machine text (the WI-3532 failure class) and floods every session's Orientation with bogus PENDING directives that agents must resolve by hand.
2. The mode-registration hook is gated on this turn classifying OWNER — a wrapped machine turn containing AUTO/ideate phrasing could register a mode as ownerDirected:true.
3. Session search provenance (`turn_origin`) marks these turns owner-typed.

## Suggested durable fix
Unwrap a leading `<pasted_content id=…>` … `</pasted_content>` (and whatever other client wrappers exist) BEFORE envelope parse + ledger hash, in ONE shared normalizer used by all 4 grammar sites (see EI-20202332205249019 — the grammar is re-typed in 4 sites/3 languages, incl. the shell form at envelope-grammar.ts:93). Recurrence guard: a unit test in turn-provenance feeding a wrapped enveloped continuation and asserting VERIFIED AGENT-ORIGIN, plus a test that a wrapped owner paste without an envelope still classifies OWNER. Consider a one-shot sweep dismissing currently-open orders whose text starts with a wrapped envelope.

Related (different leak paths, both closed): WI-38268, WI-37908.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-09-26 (su-07b72cf6, for WI-10002524 / P-521, plan D-066).

Observation: nightly 0.0.22-20260926.1031 (task 0mui91l2w1pvzp6g1dh, green main 13342a27) passed migration boot-smoke (TEST_FILE_RESULT status=passed, 63s). It then died at 10:44:29Z with "==> seed: no committed corestore to reuse — cutting FRESH from the live store (requires a quiesced operator)" / "ERROR: fresh release seed cut requires a quiesced operator; run bin/cut-seed-quiesced.sh." (journalctl --user -u pc-0mui91l2w1pvzp6g1dh.scope).

Mechanism [measured by reading code]: papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/seed is gitignored (papercusp-desktop/.gitignore:61). apps/operator/bin/release/setup-release-checkout.sh extract_submodule_source does rm -rf $RELEASE_ROOT/<submodule> and re-extracts from git archive on every fire, so an isolated cut root NEVER has a seed snapshot. release-local.sh cut_release_seed (auto mode) then falls to the fresh-from-live-store branch. That branch requires release_seed_cut_is_quiesced (a runtime marker or masked bg-host), which a managed routine never has. This has never surfaced before: the 09-24 nightly died earlier at leg start (WI-10003216) and today's 07:00Z died at boot-smoke (WI-10003218).

Fix (su-07b72cf6): release-local.sh cut_release_seed hydrates src-tauri/seed from a persistent snapshot store (PAPERCUSP_SEED_SNAPSHOT_DIR, default ~/.papercusp/release-seeds/current; empty disables) when the root has no corestore. The existing auto-reuse path then refreshes git+epoch-keys only, with no quiesce needed. Populate the store from the newest quiesced cut (papercusp-relcut-0021-current seed, cutTs 2026-09-22T07:34Z).

Impact: every managed nightly and every isolated cut root fails here until fixed. This is the P-521 candidate blocker.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-09-30 on avi-test (pc-host-3daf37098c8096b5d9e0ac72-877db740-vm, r62b 0.0.21-p318r62b), serial console (.papercusp/scratch/avi-test-serial-r62b.txt), su-be77f2f5, P-318:
- 11:16:27Z GCE start. 11:18:04Z startup-script [workspace-host-bootstrap] phase:verify-release, 11:18:51Z phase:install-runtime, 11:19:21Z phase:migrate-database + phase:configure-service.
- papercusp-desktop.socket and papercusp-workspace.service were already active at 11:18:56Z, so desktop.start succeeded: papercusp-desktop@0-694-999 started 11:18:58Z (desktop 0f9dadb3, watch probe reached desktop.ready 11:19:11Z).
- 11:19:23Z the bootstrap restarted papercusp-workspace.service. papercusp-desktop@.service has BindsTo=papercusp-workspace.service, so systemd stopped the desktop first. The customer's desktop was gone 25 s after it opened. The bootstrap completed at 11:19:54Z.
- The same restart also ends any terminal or agent session the customer opened in that window [inferred from the unit stop; not separately measured].

Impact: after any reboot, whatever a customer opens in roughly the first 3 minutes is killed without explanation. 'Units active' is not a readiness signal, which also misled the P-318 r62b avi-test acceptance script.

_claimSubjectBaseline.summary:
MEASURED 2026-09-30 on avi-test (pc-host-3daf37098c8096b5d9e0ac72-877db740-vm, r62b 0.0.21-p318r62b), serial console (.papercusp/scratch/avi-test-serial-r62b.txt), su-be77f2f5, P-318:
- 11:16:27Z GCE start. 11:18:04Z startup-script [workspace-host-bootstrap] phase:verify-release, 11:18:51Z phase:install-runtime, 11:19:21Z phase:migrate-database + phase:configure-service.
- papercusp-desktop.socket and papercusp-workspace.service were already active at 11:18:56Z, so desktop.start succeeded: papercusp-desktop@0-694-999 started 11:18:58Z (desktop 0f9dadb3, watch probe reached desktop.ready 11:19:11Z).
- 11:19:23Z the bootstrap restarted papercusp-workspace.service. papercusp-desktop@.service has BindsTo=papercusp-workspace.service, so systemd stopped the desktop first. The customer's desktop was gone 25 s after it opened. The bootstrap completed at 11:19:54Z.

admissionIdentity.titleKey: title:30s baseline cold during embed idle llama none ornith server sidecar stalls start

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[measured 2026-10-06 su-6008b, EI-25222670171204378 follow-up]
Cold-start window (llama-ornith stopped 10:01:23Z, gateway answered 10:06:36Z): 193 cache-bypassing /embed samples every 2s, median 0.053s, but 13.3s @10:01:36, 14.3s @10:04:10, 30.0s client timeout @10:04:56, 22.0s @10:07:08, 21.8s @10:08:26 (raw: docs/evidence/reboot-residue-live-probes-2026-10-06/r002-coldstart-embed-samples.tsv).
Baseline right after, ornith loaded and idle (10:11-10:15Z): 92 samples, max 1.5s, none over 5s; healthz queue never saturated.
So the stalls go with the cold start, but they begin before the GPU upload (10:01:36) and continue ~2 min after the answer, so GPU memory contention alone does not fit. Mechanism NOT established. [inferred] candidate: reading the 15.4 GB GGUF from /mnt/data evicts page cache, so the sidecar takes major faults on its model files. Distinguishing probe: sample /embed plus the sidecar's major-fault count (/proc/<pid>/stat field 12) and vmstat si/bi through a cold start; then repeat with the GGUF pre-warmed in page cache (vmtouch) — stalls that vanish point to page cache.
Impact is bounded now: the watchdog no longer restarts on a single slow probe (2-consecutive threshold, EI-25222670171204378), so a stall delays embeds but no longer takes the sidecar down.

The hive epoch was never advancing past 0 because papercusp-hive-rekey resolved false on the rig sidecar (a stale PG flag-override shadowing the compiled DEFAULT-ON — confirmed live: /api/flags/set returned backend:'pg-override', posthogFailureReason:'flag-backend-not-configured'), so advanceEpochOnHiveBoundary silently no-op'd (applied:false, no throw, and — before this fix — no stdout signal either) on every revoke. With the epoch stuck at 0, post-ban content stayed under the same key the banned member already held: not a leak in the crypto/K-cut design, a test-rig gap that left the mechanism unarmed (same class two-instance-hive-from-repo-smoke.sh already hit and fixed for its own leg, su-9140a 2026-06-19 — the deb-hetzner-*.sh rigs never got the equivalent fix).

terminalCompletionEvidence.summary:
Removed the two stale ElevenLabs-CDN scratch pages from the committed sidecar staging SPA artifact, AND corrected this item's central claim: they were never shipped. The filed title said the SPA 'still ships' them; verification of the actual ship path shows no packaged artifact ever carried them. Corrected in full in the thread comment (post 79055).

Ship-path finding: the pages sat at the TOP-LEVEL papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/env-sidecars/staging/spa/. No `resources` glob in any of the six tauri config variants covers that path — every glob is rooted at src-tauri/SIDECAR/, a different directory. What ships is generated: bin/stage-env-sidecars.sh does `rm -rf $SIDECAR/env-sidecars` then `cp -al $SIDECAR/spa $ENV_SC/spa`, hardlink-copying the PRIMARY sidecar SPA, which does not contain these pages. bin/build-windows-cross.sh independently rm -rf's and re-stages the top-level dir before building.

Root cause of the residue: that directory is a committed BUILD ARTIFACT the build regenerates. Independently corroborated by EI-20555742146560765, which measured 4,483 tracked files under the same path and 2,418 self-dirtied entries during the 0.0.17 release cut. The two pages were stale content dating to 2026-07-07, from when the primary SPA still had them.

My own instrument error, recorded so it does not recur: the initial `git ls-files | grep el-` was run from the SUPERPROJECT and returned nothing, which made tracked files look like untracked stray output. git ls-files does not recurse into submodules and papercusp-desktop is one.
